title: missing features, google != privacy, no cost != free
body:
Let’s start with a review haiku 
—-
Google scrapes your data
They sell you off for profit
Is this really free? 
—-

First off it’s a reality that probably most of us should be trying to ditch google.  It’s a company based on selling us, or our digital selves, and it’s scary. 

Most people don’t care so let’s look at what you get from this app. 

You get a basic notes app that works cross platform and is “free”. It has 3D Touch actions. That’s nice. 

The Apple notes app does everything and more this app does - but doesn’t offer real cross platform syncing.  Going to the iCloud webpage on windows doesn’t count as cross platform to me - it counts as barely usable.  

If you subscribe to Microsoft office live / 365 / whatever it’s named this week - it does everything this does and more. But in an old clunky UI they just can’t seem to abandon, without shortcuts / good widget support. It also doesn’t support markdown or have easy export to other apps 

Evernote does everything this does and has a free tier - but some may find that tier limiting.  Again it doesn’t support markdown.  

A couple things are seriously lacking for me in google keep as with others. 

No markdown support, no shortcuts integration. 

I have a couple of shortcuts setup on iOS to create a note from clipboard and ask where to file it - without launching Apple notes, for me it’s a double tap on the back of the phone.  I have another one that allows me to recall the last 10 clipboard saves and select to copy back the body from a list.  

Unfortunately nobody has come along in all this time to make a notes app that’s “right”

I need real cross platform - shortcuts integration at least to Apple notes level, markdown support. 

Ideally a quick way to send note content to any other app.  Like drafts - which would be perfect if they ever considered windows users, unfortunately most app developers live in a world where they think 90% of iOS users have MacBook Pro’s.  

So here it is - just another notes app competing to hold your data, from a company notorious for scraping it and selling off to the highest bidder.  

I’ll opt for one that does all the same things, and more, and go to iCloud to access on a pc, for now. 

I’m sure someone will make the right one soon, google doesn’t yet and the quagmire if they did would be a biggie- because I don’t trust them - or their obviously lip service informal corporate motto of don’t be evil - because frankly I shouldn’t.

title: Too limited on font size and sorting
body: In principle Google Keep is a good app. It can handle images, it has a tag facility which enables you to organise notes and view notes with a specific theme, it is cross-platform so it is not tied to Apple devices, searching is fast, and it is simple. Bits of the interface are slightly cumbersome, but this is not a serious problem. But the app has three main drawbacks. First, sorting options are virtually nonexistent. Second, there seems to be absolutely no control over fonts and font sizes, and on an iPad mini you need good eyesight to read notes comfortably. Third, there is a size limit for notes - above a certain size the app requires you to use Google docs, but there is no integration with Google docs.

title: Does not work the same way as the online version
body:
Google have crippled this app by removing the List Setting feature of the online version. This means that lists I've have previously written online behave differently in the app. I had set my lists so that ticked items move to the bottom, and the rest stay at the top. In the app, ticked items stay where they are, and there is no way to change that. This is a problem for me when writing shopping. I can't see why the app and online versions need to behave differently. 

Also, both versions need a feature that allows lists to be reordered alphabetically and/or numerically.
